text:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] paged-attention allocator fragmentation rising on pool=inf-prod-eu-3. Node group=ng-infer-3 reporting repeated container restarts and CUDA OOMs. Affected service: model-worker (v2.3.1). p99 /v1/generate latency up from 1.8s -> 4.5s, some 5xx spikes. Marking sev2. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/paged-allocator-frag
jun kim: Ack. Is there a new deploy around the window? saw restart flurry ~10:11 UTC.
maria ramos: No deploys. Trend shows steady memory RSS creep on gpu nodes since ~09:45. Logs show repeated failures to unmap bitmap pages: "bitmap_unmap: unmap failed, remaining 12 segments".
dev-runtime: grabbing logs now. attaching tail from one pod:
```
2026-03-15T09:58:12Z model-worker[pid=1823]: kv_page_fault: page_count=1024, frag=0.87
2026-03-15T09:58:15Z model-worker[pid=1823]: cuda_call: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (2)
2026-03-15T09:58:15Z model-worker[pid=1823]: killing process due to OOM
```
jun kim: ok. Possible causes: allocator bitmap fragmentation + stale KVpages on long-lived sessions. We saw similar slow-creep pattern last quarter but that was fixed by slab defrag and lowering KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD.
ops-lead: immediate mitigations I can do: 1) shift traffic off pool inf-prod-eu-3 to eu-1/asia temporarily 2) enable fallback to quantized-model-v2 on heavy routes 3) cordon & drain the 2 worst nodes and restart workers there.
sre-rotating: suggest also toggling aggressive-defrag mode on restarted pods. There is a hot flag: ENABLE_SLAB_DEFRAG=true (non-disruptive on restart). Use careful rollout to avoid CPU spikes.
jun kim: steps then: A) add route fallback (ops-lead) B) cordon+drain two nodes (sre-rotating) C) restart model-worker pods with ENABLE_SLAB_DEFRAG=true and KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.7 (dev-runtime) D) enable additional metrics: kv.pages.evicted, kv.pages.in_use, allocator.bitmap_frag
maria ramos: note: evict threshold default was 0.9 in this pool (too high). lowering to 0.7 should force earlier evictions and reduce fragmentation growth.
dev-runtime: commands I'm running now (will paste output):
```
# mark node unschedulable and drain
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-32.eu-west-1
kubectl drain ip-10-0-5-32.eu-west-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
# set env for deployment so new pods restart with defrag
kubectl set env deployment/model-worker ENABLE_SLAB_DEFRAG=true KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.7 -n prod
# rollout restart to pick up env
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-worker -n prod
```
ops-lead: patching traffic router now to cascade fallback for /v1/generate to quantized-model-v2 for 25% of traffic then ramp down to 0 on inf-prod-eu-3.
customer-success: reached out to two customers with heavy traffic patterns (acct: AcmeCorp, acct: NovaApps). Notified them of possible latency/5xx and that we are doing mitigation. No SLAs breached yet but monitoring closely.
sre-rotating: drain succeeded on ip-10-0-5-32, ip-10-0-5-44 also cordoned. pods rescheduled to eu-1. Observed one immediate reduction in OOMs on drained nodes.
jun kim: after restart we should watch these metrics for 30m: allocator.bitmap_frag, kv.page_fault_rate, gpu.memory_used, p99_latency. If fragmentation continues to grow -> take pool offline and roll full pod restart with defrag + heap dump analysis.
dev-runtime: rollout finished, new pods coming up with ENABLE_SLAB_DEFRAG=true. Early logs show defrag worker running: "slab_defrag: reclaimed 18 pages in 120s".
```
2026-03-15T10:08:41Z defrag: reclaimed=18 pages, time_ms=120000
```
sre-rotating: seeing evictions increase (expected) but page_fault_rate down by ~35% over 5m.
maria ramos: memory RSS growth rate slowed in sampled nodes. Good sign.
ops-lead: routing adjusted: inf-prod-eu-3 now at 10% traffic, quantized fallback at 30% for heavy routes. Rolling toward normal if metrics hold.
customer-success: updated customers, they acknowledged. one asked for postmortem if we degrade further.
jun kim: plan for followup: 1) continue monitoring 2) collect heap dumps from 2 affected pods (dev-runtime) 3) run offline defrag analyzer against dump to identify hot allocation patterns 4) schedule infra change to lower default KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD for this pool in prod config if confirmed.
dev-runtime: started heap dump: /var/log/model-worker/heapdump-1769990000-1.tar.gz (uploaded to internal S3: s3://internal-heapdumps/1769990000-1)
sre-rotating: set alert thresholds tighter: kv.page_fault_rate > 50/min -> page the oncall.
jun kim: handing off to night oncall @sre-rotating at 2026-03-15T12:00 UTC. Handoff notes: mitigations applied (drains, env flag, lowered evict threshold), current state: p99 latency trending down, OOMs reduced, evictions increased. Watchlist: bitmap_frag, page_fault_rate, 5xx rate. If re-escalates -> take pool offline and failover.
sre-rotating: got it. added short summary to incident board and set a follow-up ticket to run deeper allocator analysis (infra-ticket #INF-4823).
oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident annotated: mitigation actions recorded. Next update at +30m.
jun kim: thumbs up everyone, nice triage. :thumbsup:
